note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Introduction and Key Definitions
explain: Time of supply fixes the exact point in time when GST liability arises.
Tax payment due dates are calculated with reference to the time of supply.
Goods under Section 2(52) include movable property, actionable claims, and growing crops, but exclude money and securities.
Services under Section 2(102) cover anything other than goods, money, and securities, including money usage or conversion for separate consideration.
Recipient under Section 2(93) is the person liable to pay consideration, or the person receiving goods/services if no consideration is payable.

flow.title: Determining Recipient of Supply
steps: Check if consideration is payable for supply
If yes, recipient is person paying consideration
If no consideration for goods, person receiving goods
If no consideration for services, person rendered service
Include agent acting on behalf of recipient

topics.example: A company orders office supplies for an employee and pays the invoice directly. The company is the recipient because it pays the consideration.
remember: Time of supply marks tax liability creation, not necessarily the payment deadline.
Actionable claims are included in goods, while securities are excluded from both goods and services.
mistakes: Confusing time of supply with the due date of filing monthly returns.
Treating securities as goods or services under GST.

quiz.q: What indicates the exact point in time when GST liability arises?
quiz.why: Time of supply fixes the point in time when tax liability arises.

quiz.q: Which of the following is specifically included in the definition of goods under Section 2(52)?
quiz.why: Goods include actionable claims, growing crops, and grass, but exclude money and securities.

topics.title: Time of Supply of Goods under Forward Charge
explain: Under Section 12(2), time of supply of goods is the date of invoice or the last date to issue invoice under Section 31.
By Notification No. 66/2017 CT, taxpayers (except composition dealers and specified actionable claim suppliers) do not pay GST on advances received for goods.
Invoice must be issued before or at the time of removal of goods where movement is involved.
If movement is not involved, invoice must be issued at the time of delivery or making goods available.
For continuous supply of goods under Section 31(4), invoice is due on or before issuance of periodic statement or receipt of payment.

flow.title: Forward Charge TOS for Goods
steps: Check date of tax invoice issuance
Find last date required u/s 31
Compare invoice date and last required date
Select earlier of the two dates
Ignore advance payment date per Notification 66/2017

topics.example: A manufacturer dispatches goods on 5th September and issues invoice on the same date. Advance payment was received on 21st August. Time of supply is 5th September.
remember: No GST on advance received for supply of goods under forward charge.
Invoice deadline for goods sent on approval is 6 months from removal or time of supply, whichever is earlier.
mistakes: Calculating GST liability on advance payment received for forward charge supply of goods.
Missing the 6-month deadline for goods sent on approval or sale basis.

quiz.q: Under forward charge, what is the time of supply of goods for regular suppliers receiving an advance?
o: Date of invoice or last date required to issue invoice
Date of bank entry of final payment
quiz.why: Notification No. 66/2017 exempts advance received for goods under forward charge from GST.

quiz.q: What is the maximum time limit to issue an invoice for goods sent on approval basis under Section 31(7)?
o: 6 months from removal or time of supply, whichever is earlier
quiz.why: Section 31(7) specifies invoice must be issued at time of supply or 6 months from removal, whichever is earlier.

topics.title: Time of Supply of Goods under Reverse Charge
explain: Under Section 12(3), time of supply for goods under RCM is the earliest of three dates.
First: Date of physical receipt of goods.
Second: Date of payment recorded in recipient's books or debited in bank account, whichever is earlier.
Third: Date immediately following 30 days from supplier's invoice date (i.e., 31st day).
If none of these can be determined, time of supply is the date of entry of goods in recipient's books of account.

flow.title: RCM TOS for Goods Determination
steps: Identify date of receipt of goods
Identify date of payment by recipient
Calculate 31st day from supplier invoice
Compare all three available dates
Take the earliest of the dates
If unascertainable, take recipient book entry date

topics.example: Supplier invoices RCM goods on 4th May. Goods received on 12th May. Payment made on 30th May. The 31st day is 4th June. Time of supply is 12th May.
remember: Advance payment exemption does NOT apply to goods under reverse charge.
Use the 31st day from the invoice date, not 30th day.
mistakes: Applying Notification No. 66/2017 to exempt RCM advances on goods.
Counting 60 days instead of 30 days for goods under RCM.

quiz.q: In case of RCM on goods, what is the invoice deadline parameter to compare for time of supply?
quiz.why: Section 12(3)(c) specifies date immediately following 30 days (31st day) from supplier's invoice.

quiz.q: If RCM goods are invoiced on May 4, received on June 12, and paid on July 3, what is the time of supply? (30 days elapses June 3)
quiz.why: June 4 is the 31st day from invoice date, which is earlier than receipt (June 12) and payment (July 3).

topics.title: Time of Supply of Goods: Residual Cases & Addition in Value
explain: If time of supply cannot be determined under forward charge or reverse charge, residual provisions under Section 12(5) apply.
Where a periodic return has to be filed, time of supply is the due date of filing such return.
In any other case, time of supply is the date on which GST is paid.
Under Section 12(6), addition in value due to interest, late fee, or penalty for delayed consideration has a separate time of supply.
Time of supply for such additional value is the exact date on which the supplier receives the addition in value.

flow.title: Residual & Addition Value TOS Process
steps: Check if main TOS rules apply
If not, check if periodic return is required
If return required, TOS is return due date
If no return required, TOS is tax payment date
For interest/late fee additions, TOS is date received

topics.example: Goods sold on 6th June with 2% interest per month for late payment. Interest of ₹2,000 received on 6th July. TOS for ₹2,000 interest is 6th July.
remember: Interest/late fee addition in value is taxed on receipt basis.
Residual cases apply only when sub-sections (2), (3), or (4) cannot determine TOS.
mistakes: Treating interest on delayed payment as taxable on the original invoice date.
Using tax payment date when a periodical return due date exists.

quiz.q: What is the time of supply for interest or late fee received for delayed payment of consideration for goods?
o: Date on which supplier receives addition in value
Due date of return for the month of sale
quiz.why: Section 12(6) states TOS for interest/late fee is the date on which supplier receives such addition in value.

quiz.q: Under Section 12(5), if a periodic return is required to be filed, what is the time of supply in residual cases?
o: Due date on which such return is to be filed
quiz.why: Section 12(5)(a) mandates due date of filing periodic return as the time of supply.

topics.title: Time of Supply of Services under Forward Charge
explain: Under Section 13(2), TOS of service depends on whether invoice is issued within the prescribed time limit under Section 31(2) read with Rule 47.
Prescribed invoice limit is 30 days from service completion (45 days for banks, insurance companies, and NBFCs).
If invoice is issued within time limit: TOS is earlier of date of issue of invoice OR date of receipt of payment.
If invoice is NOT issued within time limit: TOS is earlier of date of provision of service OR date of receipt of payment.
If both methods fail, TOS is the date recipient shows receipt of service in their books.
Option for excess payment up to ₹1,000: Supplier can opt to take date of next invoice as TOS for the excess amount.

flow.title: Forward Charge TOS for Services
steps: Check date of completion of service
Check if invoice issued within 30/45 days
If YES: Earliest of invoice date & payment date
If NO: Earliest of service date & payment date
If unknown: Date recipient records service in books

topics.example: Consultancy completed 15th Sept. Invoice raised 20th Sept (within 30 days). Payment received 10th Oct. TOS is 20th Sept.
remember: Unlike goods, advance payment for services IS subject to GST on receipt date.
Banking and insurance sector gets 45 days to issue tax invoice instead of 30 days.
mistakes: Assuming advance received for services is exempt from GST at receipt stage.
Using invoice date when invoice was issued after the 30-day limit.

quiz.q: If consultancy service provided on Sept 15 is invoiced on Oct 25 (after 30 days) and paid Oct 30, what is the TOS?
quiz.why: Since invoice was not issued within 30 days, TOS is earlier of provision of service (Sept 15) or payment (Oct 30).

quiz.q: What is the prescribed time limit to issue invoice for services by a banking company under Rule 47?
quiz.why: Rule 47 provides a 45-day invoice window for insurance, banking companies, and financial institutions.

topics.title: Time of Supply of Services under Reverse Charge & Associated Enterprises
explain: Under Section 13(3), TOS for services under RCM is the earlier of payment date or date immediately following 60 days from supplier's invoice date (61st day).
Payment date means date of payment entry in recipient's books or bank debit date, whichever is earlier.
If invoice is to be issued by recipient u/s 31(3)(f), TOS is date of issue of invoice by recipient (must be within 30 days of service receipt).
If dates cannot be determined, TOS is date of entry of service in recipient's books of account.
For import of service from Associated Enterprise outside India: TOS is earlier of date of payment OR date of entry in recipient's books.

flow.title: RCM Services TOS Determination
steps: Check date of payment entry or bank debit
Calculate 61st day from supplier invoice
Check recipient invoice date if applicable
Compare available dates and take earliest
If Associated Enterprise import: Earlier of payment & recipient book entry

topics.example: Advocate firm invoices legal services on 17th Feb. Payment made on 3rd Nov. The 61st day from invoice is 19th April. TOS is 19th April.
remember: RCM parameter for service invoice gap is 60 days (61st day), compared to 30 days (31st day) for goods.
For associated enterprise imports, 60 days rule does not apply; book entry vs payment date applies.
mistakes: Confusing 31st day rule for goods RCM with 61st day rule for service RCM.
Applying the 60-day rule to imports from associated enterprises.

quiz.q: What is the benchmark day following supplier invoice date for RCM services under Section 13(3)?
quiz.why: Section 13(3)(b) states date immediately following 60 days (61st day) from date of issue of invoice.

quiz.q: For import of services from an Associated Enterprise located outside India, what is the TOS?
o: Earlier of date of entry in recipient's books or date of payment
quiz.why: Proviso to Section 13(3) prescribes TOS as earlier of book entry date of recipient or payment date.

topics.title: Time of Supply of Services: Residual Cases & Addition in Value
explain: Where TOS for services cannot be determined under sub-sections (2), (3), or (4), residual rules of Section 13(5) apply.
If a periodical return is required to be filed, TOS is the due date of filing such return.
In any other case, TOS is the date on which GST is paid.
Under Section 13(6), addition in value due to interest, late fee, or penalty for delayed payment of service consideration has a distinct TOS.
TOS for such addition in value is the date on which the supplier receives the addition in value.

flow.title: Services Residual & Value Addition Flow
steps: Confirm main service TOS rules cannot be applied
Check requirement of periodical return
If periodic return required, TOS = Return due date
If no return required, TOS = Tax payment date
For interest/late fee, TOS = Date supplier receives payment

topics.example: A telecom operator receives ₹500 as late fee on 15th August for overdue July bill. TOS for ₹500 late fee is 15th August.
remember: Residual and addition-in-value provisions are identical for both goods and services.
Addition in value is always recognized on receipt basis.
mistakes: Accruing interest/late fee for GST TOS before actual receipt.
Diverging between goods and services rules for interest on late payment.

quiz.q: When is GST payable on late fee received for delayed payment of service consideration under Section 13(6)?
o: Date supplier receives such addition in value
quiz.why: Section 13(6) fixes TOS on the date the supplier receives the additional amount.

quiz.q: In residual cases under Section 13(5), if no periodical return is required to be filed, what is the TOS?
o: Date on which tax is paid
quiz.why: Section 13(5)(b) specifies the date on which tax is paid as TOS in non-return residual cases.
